title: The Hidden Challenge of a Highly Cohesive Team
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece flags an overlooked risk in high-trust, tight-knit teams: their very closeness can suppress candid feedback and make them insular toward outside expertise. It argues that deep caring between teammates can make people reluctant to raise hard issues for fear of damaging the goodwill they've built. Highly cohesive teams are also described as prone to dismissing outside consultants and data, creating blind spots. The article treats this as a manageable 'quality problem' rather than a fundamental flaw, solvable by naming the risk early.
points: Highly cohesive teams risk suppressing candid feedback because members fear damaging close relationships.
Deep trust can make teams insular, avoiding outside experts and data that could help.
This vulnerability is described as a 'quality problem' most teams would be glad to have.
Naming the risk explicitly, early, is often enough to prevent it from taking hold.
A commitment to consistent feedback and outside counsel should be built into the team charter from the start.
quotes: The extreme caring and comfort a close-knit team experiences can hinder honesty and prevent them from seeking outside help.
Highly cohesive teams are often allergic to outside voices, consultants, and other external experts who can bring them data and insight.
This desire for harmony can inhibit the willingness of team members to discuss issues openly and honestly.
Of course, guarding against the downside of being a highly cohesive and trustful team is a quality problem most teams would die for.
Team members who like each other a lot need to commit to open and direct communication in all directions.
